concepts: object detection, shape transformation, frame sequencing, text overlay, color consistency
description: In the input you will see a single orange-haired puppet (bulging white eyes, open mouth) with its yellow-orange arms hanging down against a blurred brown-metallic barred background. There is no text in the input. The puppet’s facial features and background bars remain static. To make the output: 1. Detect and isolate the puppet sprite (hair, eyes, mouth, torso, arms) on the non-black background. 2. Create three side-by-side “frames” by replicating the entire input grid horizontally three times. 3. In the first (leftmost) frame, leave the puppet exactly as in the input (arms down). 4. In the second (middle) frame, raise the puppet’s arms by moving every arm pixel up by 2 cells, preserving arm shape and color. 5. In the third (rightmost) frame, raise the arms a further 2 pixels (total of 4 up), and slightly enlarge the mouth by adding one pixel row to the lower lip. 6. Overlay bold white uppercase text “I’M FREEEE” centered just above the puppet’s head only in the third frame. 7. Keep the background bars and all original colors unchanged behind each puppet copy.
visual_elements: Orange-haired puppet with bulging white eyes and open mouth
Yellow-orange puppet body and outstretched arms
Bold white uppercase text overlay reading “I’M FREEEE”
Blurred brown and metallic background with structural bars
High contrast between puppet’s bright colors and darker background
static_patterns: Puppet’s facial features (hair shape, eye size, mouth shape) remain constant
Background elements (bars, walls, lighting) do not move
Text font style and on-screen position stay the same when visible
Color palette of puppet (orange, yellow) remains unchanged
dynamic_patterns: Puppet raises and flails arms upward in a rapid motion
Head bobs forward and tilts back repeatedly
Mouth opens wider in sync with each head movement
Text overlay appears immediately as the puppet’s motion peaks
Frame-by-frame positional shift toward camera indicates a jump or lunge
core_principles: Exaggerated limb movement conveys emotional intensity
Synchronization of visual motion and text reinforces message
Sequential frame updates create the illusion of continuous action
Cause-and-effect linkage: muscle-like joint articulation drives arm flail
The most fundamental principle is that rapid succession of slightly different frames produces the perception of motion.
